source.author: lucr
source.text: cetera quae fieri in terris caeloque tuentur mortales, pavidis cum pendent mentibus saepe et faciunt animos humilis formidine divom depressosque premunt ad terram propterea quod ignorantia causarum conferre deorum cogit ad imperium res et concedere regnum.
source.text_original: cetera quae fieri in terris caeloque tuentur / mortales, pavidis cum pendent mentibus saepe / et faciunt animos humilis formidine divom / depressosque premunt ad terram propterea quod / ignorantia causarum conferre deorum / cogit ad imperium res et concedere regnum.
source.text_english: The other things which mortals observe to happen on earth and in heaven they often watch with fearful minds, and, cowering, they keep their spirits oppressed and crushed to the ground by base fear of the gods, because ignorance of causes compels them to attribute events to the will of the gods and to surrender sovereignty to them.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: ait enim: et faciunt animos humiles formidine diuum depressosque premunt ad terram.
reuse.text_original: ait enim: et faciunt animos humiles formidine diuum depressosque premunt ad terram.
reuse.text_english: For he says: and they make minds humbled, cast down by fear of the gods, and they press them down to the earth.
